LIFECYCLE EXPERIMENTS / v0.1.9 / 2026-11-13

1,140 scripted trials. Every cleanup inside its declared bound.

We ran the published v0.1.9 binaries on native macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64: expiry, killed supervisors, an interrupted launcher with blocked output, and keyed retries. An independent observer decided each cleanup by watching the service processes and their port, not by asking ProcLease. All 570 trials on each platform passed. The total includes 1,020 product trials and 120 observer controls. These figures come from the primary series, run with the amended observer of protocol version 2. An earlier series with the first observer also passed and stays published separately. These are scripted host CLI tests, not agent sessions, and not a benchmark.

Recorded state is kept apart from observed cleanup. After a keeper SIGKILL every group was cleaned up, yet no record carried the keeper's finalization marker, because that keeper was gone. After a guardian SIGKILL, all 60 did.

03 / METHOD

Real binaries. Independent observation.

  • Release archives were checked against the published SHA256SUMS; the extracted binaries reported proclease 0.1.9. Nothing was built from source.
  • A Python standard-library harness ran the same protocol on both hosts. Protocol version 2 and the published harness were frozen, with recorded hashes, before the primary runs. Smoke runs are not counted, and no trial was retried or discarded.
  • Each trial had its own private state directory, temporary directory and synthetic environment. The service was a small HTTP fixture: a parent and a forked child in one process group.
  • Cleanup counted only after the observer had first seen both processes running, the same process group and the HTTP marker. It then required each process to be absent or exited (unreaped) and the port to refuse connections.
  • A failed or denied process listing is recorded as an error, never as absence. A live PID whose command no longer shows the trial token is never counted as stopped; the observer keeps polling.
  • Supervisors and launchers were signalled only after their current command line identified this trial's job. Saved PIDs were never signalled on their own.

04 / LIMITS

What these trials do not show.

  • No agent took part. Codex and Claude Code compatibility, sandbox profiles and application servers such as Vite or Next.js are outside these results.
  • Cleanup was checked for a parent and one same-group child. A descendant that starts its own session or process group can escape ProcLease cleanup; no containment is claimed.
  • Thirty repetitions cannot rule out rarer failures. Sleep and wake, clock changes, destroying both supervisors at once and whole-sandbox teardown were not tested.
  • In 10 of 420 exit observations on macOS and 22 of 420 on Linux, a live PID briefly showed a command without the trial token. The harness cannot tell an exiting process from PID reuse, so it waited until each was absent or exited.
  • The observer sees processes and the port, not signals. TERM-ignoring services surviving the grace does not show the signal order.

The first counted series used an observer that ignored ps failures and counted 21 such samples as stopped. It also passed 570 of 570 trials per platform, but it is kept as a separate, earlier dataset. The primary series repeated every trial with the amended observer.
